value.name: Charlene criticizes the movie choice
value.description: After leaving the theater, Charlene complains that the movie Micky chose was disappointing and questions who recommended it.
evidence: After the movie, Micky and Charlene exit the theater.
CHARLENE asks, 'That's what you wanted to see? There wasn't even any sex. What Lowell guy on a road crew saw that movie in Lexington and recommended it??'

value.name: Micky fumbles for his keys
value.description: Micky rushes toward the car, cannot find his keys, and becomes visibly anxious before realizing he is holding them.
evidence: Micky walks quickly ahead to the car, can't find his keys.
MICKY grows anxious, muttering, 'Where's the keys, I musta lost 'em in the theatah, I'm a dummy,' as he turns back toward the theater.
CHARLENE calls out, 'Micky,' and he stops, turns. 'They're in your hand.'
Micky looks down, embarrassed to see the keys clenched in his fist.

value.name: Charlene questions Micky's secrecy
value.description: At the car, Charlene confronts Micky about whether he is avoiding a girlfriend and why he brought her to Lexington.
evidence: At the 1989 silver Ford Tempo, Charlene stares at him as he starts the car.
He begins to back out, looking over his shoulder.
CHARLENE presses, 'What's going on? You afraid to run into your girlfriend? You have a girlfriend, just say it, that's why you took me to Lexington.'

value.name: Micky admits shame about returning home
value.description: Micky stops the car and admits he came to Lexington because he does not want to face people in Lowell.
evidence: He suddenly stops, puts the car in park, and turns the engine off.
MICKY insists, 'I don't have a girlfriend. I came here because I don't wanna show my face in Lowell.'

value.name: Micky reveals his failed expectations
value.description: Micky explains that he feels ashamed because he promised to win his fight, get back on track, and build a bigger life with Kasie.
evidence: MICKY grows dark: 'I told everyone I was gonna win that fight and get back on track. I told Kasie we'd get a biggah place so she could move in.'

value.name: Charlene blames his family for the fight
value.description: Charlene reminds Micky that he said his mother and brother pushed him into the fight he now regrets.
evidence: CHARLENE replies, 'You said you never shoulda fought that guy, but your mothah and your brothah wanted ya to do it.'

value.name: Micky rejects being alone in the ring
value.description: Micky snaps that the blame does not matter because he feels isolated when he fights.
evidence: MICKY snaps, 'What's the difference, I'm alone in the ring anyway.'

value.name: Charlene challenges his family's loyalty
value.description: Charlene pushes Micky to confront whether his family is truly looking out for him.
evidence: CHARLENE challenges, 'You think your family's lookin' out for ya?'

value.name: Micky defends his family
value.description: Micky insists Charlene cannot speak badly about his family, showing his loyalty despite his frustration.
evidence: Finally, Micky looks at her. 'You can't say that about my family.'

value.name: Charlene confronts Micky's self-image
value.description: Charlene responds that his injuries and appearance make her question his family's support and his situation.
evidence: She holds his gaze.
What else could I say after what you told me? Look at your face, look at you.'

value.name: Micky kisses Charlene
value.description: Micky suddenly leans in and kisses Charlene, turning the confrontation into a moment of intense romantic connection.
evidence: He suddenly leans in and kisses her.
The kiss builds with confidence and passion, escalating into a moment of intense connection, abandon, and unspoken promise.
